I added the seam to `src/utils.ts`. It's one new function, `withoutHost`, placed after `withoutFragment` and written in the same doc-comment style (`@example`, `@group utils`). Its body is `throw new Error("not implemented");`. `src/index.ts` needed no change because it already does `export * from "./utils"`. The type check passes, and the existing suite still passes (13 files, 424 tests). The only file changed is `src/utils.ts`.

**Decision for you:** I wrote `withoutHost(input: string): string` with an explicit return type, although the spec says the return type should be inferred and an explicit `: string` was considered and rejected. I added it because, with a body that only throws, TypeScript infers `void`. Without it, the contract would give both test suites the wrong type. Once the real body is written it returns a string, so the implementer can remove the annotation and the inferred type will still be `string`.

Added: `withoutHost`

public.finalText:
I wrote the test suite in `test/ufo-without-host-confirmed.test.ts`. Each of the 15 scenarios in the spec gets two flat tests: a happy path and one boundary case. Each test name starts with the scenario's key: `[happy-1..3]`, `[boundary-1..10]` and `[unhappy-1..2]`.

**Checks run:**
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors. That config only covers `src`, so I also type-checked the test file on its own, which was clean with `--skipLibCheck`.
- `npx vitest run test/ufo-without-host-confirmed.`: 29 tests fail and 1 passes, as expected while the body throws. The one that passes is `[happy-2] the entry point re-exports the same function as src/utils`. It only checks that `src/index.ts` exports the same function as `src/utils.ts`, so it doesn't depend on the body.
- I also ran every expected value against a throwaway reference built on `parseURL`, using the spec's own definition. All 30 passed there, so the expected values agree with how `parseURL` actually splits each input. The reference lives only in the scratchpad.

**What's covered:**
- The happy paths and most boundary cases come straight from the spec's example tables.
- Four boundary inputs are not in the spec's tables:
  - a backslash-only path after the host (`https:\\example.com\` → `/`)
  - a leading tab and newline before the protocol
  - several leading NUL characters
  - calling with `""` twice to check it's stable

  Each of these follows from a rule the spec states.
- For the backslash cases, the source escapes each backslash in the input (`"https:\\\\example.com\\foo\\bar"`), so the string tested is the spec's literal `https:\\example.com\foo\bar`.

The only file I added is the test file. Nothing in `src/`, the config files or the existing tests changed.

30 tests, in 1 file.

private.finalText:
I wrote the hidden suite in `test/hidden-ufo-without-host-confirmed/without-host.test.ts`. Against the current stub, all 41 tests fail with `not implemented`, and `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors.

**How I checked the expected values:** I ran a temporary copy of the suite against a small reference built straight from the spec's definition, `(parseURL(input).pathname || "/") + search + hash`. All 41 tests passed against it. I then deleted the reference and its copy, so the folder now holds only the test file.

**Coverage:**
- **Scenarios:** every one has tests: happy 1–3, boundary 1–10 and unhappy 1–2. Every table row the public suite leaves out is a test of its own, for example `https://example.com/foo?q=123`, `[::1]`, `HTTP://Example.COM/Foo`, the `über` row, `a?b=c?d#e#f`, `tel:123`, `data:text/plain,hi`, `http://example.com:8080` and `http://user@example.com`.
- **Extensions:** each public test has at least one test that goes further, with a comment above it naming the public test. They use other protocols, deeper paths, more combinations of credentials, port, search and hash, and backslashes in the search and hash.
- **Shortcuts targeted:**
  - **Cutting at the first `@`, `/` or `://`:** `/a@b`, `?a=/b/c`, `#a?b/c`, and `?to=http://other.com/x`.
  - **Removing the first segment of host-less input as if it were a host:** `foo.com/foo?...` and `example.com` must come back unchanged.
  - **Splitting `?` and `#` off script protocols:** `javascript:alert('?x#y')`, `data:...a?b#c`, and `javascript://example.com/...` (the `//` must not be read as a host).
  - **Returning the search and hash for other protocols:** `custom:foo?x#y` and `mailto:...?subject=hi#x` must still give `/`.
  - **Making the function idempotent:** applying it repeatedly must keep stripping a leading segment.
  - **Normalising the output:** case, trailing slashes, `%2520`, `+`, `./` and `../`, and empty `?` and `#` must all be kept.

**Left out on purpose:**
- `withoutHost("javascript:")`: the definition gives `/`, but the rule says "without an added leading slash", so the spec contradicts itself here.
- Leading spaces before a protocol-relative input.
- A drive letter in a non-file URL.

41 tests in 1 file.

Open in the spec: none
